_about: Baseline test set for Document Retrieval. Every case is grounded in text that
actually exists in the demo corpus — a fabricated expectation measures nothing.
`expect_docs` is the document that OWNS the answer (its SSOT page where there is
one). `expect_phrases` are accent-folded substring probes: they check that the
retrieved passage really contains the answer, not merely that the right document
was reached, because a document-level hit with the wrong passage still produces a
Categories with no case yet are listed in `_pending` rather than faked.

identifier_lookup exists because relaxing the keyword branch to OR was first measured on question-shaped cases only, reported zero regressions, and then degraded a bare identifier lookup that no case covered. A test set that contains only one query shape certifies only that shape.

Cases are authored against published_body(), NOT the working draft: retrieval indexes the PUBLISHED version snapshot. Doc 26 is at draft v4 while v2 is live, and a probe taken from the draft failed for a system behaving exactly as designed.
expect_absent_phrases asserts text that must NOT be retrievable — the only way to test a boundary rather than a capability.

A dropped case is worth recording: 'stale-draft-only-warning' asserted that a draft-only warning callout was unreachable, but the same sentence exists in doc 25's PUBLISHED body, so the probe tested nothing about drafts. An absence probe is only valid when the text is unique to the excluded version.

metric_ssot cases are the decisive test for the governance graph: the phrase 'Gross Merchandise Value' appears in the GLOSSARY document (30) while the document that DEFINES GMV is 26. Text search sends a reader to the glossary; only GovernMetric.home_doc_id sends them to the definition.

A case may declare `scopes` to limit which suites run it. The scanned and contradictory fixtures live in their own space and are attached to no dashboard, so they exist only in the all-published suite; running them against the dashboard scope would score a document that is correctly out of reach.
